transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, let — let me say, Bob, thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And thanks to Hofstra.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, by the way, our beloved Nancy Reagan is in the hospital tonight, so our thoughts and prayers are going with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s good to see you again, Senator Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Americans are hurting right now, and they’re angry.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They’re hurting, and they’re angry.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They’re innocent victims of greed and excess on Wall Street and as well as Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And they’re angry, and they have every reason to be angry.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And they want this country to go in a new direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And there are elements of my proposal that you just outlined which I won’t repeat.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But we also have to have a short-term fix, in my view, and long- term fixes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let me just talk to you about one of the short-term fixes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The catalyst for this housing crisis was the Fannie and Freddie Mae that caused subprime lending situation that now caused the housing market in America to collapse.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I am convinced that, until we reverse this continued decline in home ownership and put a floor under it, and so that people have not only the hope and belief they can stay in their homes and realize the American dream, but that value will come up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, we have allocated $750 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s take 300 of that billion and go in and buy those home loan mortgages and negotiate with those people in their homes, 11 million homes or more, so that they can afford to pay the mortgage, stay in their home.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, I know the criticism of this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, what about the citizen that stayed in their homes?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That paid their mortgage payments?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It doesn’t help that person in their home if the next door neighbor’s house is abandoned.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And so we’ve got to reverse this.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We ought to put the homeowners first.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I am disappointed that Secretary Paulson and others have not made that their first priority.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, I want to thank Hofstra University and the people of New York for hosting us tonight and it’s wonderful to join Senator McCain again, and thank you, Bob.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think everybody understands at this point that we are experiencing the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the financial rescue plan that Senator McCain and I supported is an important first step.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I pushed for some core principles: making sure that taxpayer can get their money back if they’re putting money up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Making sure that CEOs are not enriching themselves through this process.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think that it’s going to take some time to work itself out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what we haven’t yet seen is a rescue package for the middle class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because the fundamentals of the economy were weak even before this latest crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So I’ve proposed four specific things that I think can help.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number one, let’s focus on jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to end the tax breaks for companies that are shipping jobs overseas and provide a tax credit for every company that’s creating a job right here in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number two, let’s help families right away by providing them a tax cut — a middle-class tax cut for people making less than $200,000, and let’s allow them to access their IRA accounts without penalty if they’re experiencing a crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now Senator McCain and I agree with your idea that we’ve got to help homeowners.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we included in the financial package a proposal to get homeowners in a position where they can renegotiate their mortgages.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I disagree with Senator McCain in how to do it, because the way Senator McCain has designed his plan, it could be a giveaway to banks if we’re buying full price for mortgages that now are worth a lot less.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we don’t want to waste taxpayer money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to get the financial package working much quicker than it has been working.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Last point I want to make, though.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got some long-term challenges in this economy that have to be dealt with.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to fix our energy policy that’s giving our wealth away.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to fix our health care system and we’ve got to invest in our education system for every young person to be able to learn.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I would like to mention that a couple days ago Senator Obama was out in Ohio and he had an encounter with a guy who’s a plumber, his name is Joe Wurzelbacher.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Joe wants to buy the business that he has been in for all of these years, worked 10, 12 hours a day.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And he wanted to buy the business but he looked at your tax plan and he saw that he was going to pay much higher taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You were going to put him in a higher tax bracket which was going to increase his taxes, which was going to cause him not to be able to employ people, which Joe was trying to realize the American dream.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now Senator Obama talks about the very, very rich.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Joe, I want to tell you, I’ll not only help you buy that business that you worked your whole life for and be able — and I’ll keep your taxes low and I’ll provide available and affordable health care for you and your employees.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I will not have — I will not stand for a tax increase on small business income.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Fifty percent of small business income taxes are paid by small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s 16 million jobs in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And what you want to do to Joe the plumber and millions more like him is have their taxes increased and not be able to realize the American dream of owning their own business.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s what Joe believes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He has been watching ads of Senator McCain’s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you what I’m actually going to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think tax policy is a major difference between Senator McCain and myself.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we both want to cut taxes, the difference is who we want to cut taxes for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator McCain, the centerpiece of his economic proposal is to provide $200 billion in additional tax breaks to some of the wealthiest corporations in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Exxon Mobil, and other oil companies, for example, would get an additional $4 billion in tax breaks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What I’ve said is I want to provide a tax cut for 95 percent of working Americans, 95 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you make more — if you make less than a quarter million dollars a year, then you will not see your income tax go up, your capital gains tax go up, your payroll tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Not one dime.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And 95 percent of working families, 95 percent of you out there, will get a tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In fact, independent studies have looked at our respective plans and have concluded that I provide three times the amount of tax relief to middle-class families than Senator McCain does.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, the conversation I had with Joe the plumber, what I essentially said to him was, “Five years ago, when you were in a position to buy your business, you needed a tax cut then.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” And what I want to do is to make sure that the plumber, the nurse, the firefighter, the teacher, the young entrepreneur who doesn’t yet have money, I want to give them a tax break now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that requires us to make some important choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The last point I’ll make about small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Not only do 98 percent of small businesses make less than $250,000, but I also want to give them additional tax breaks, because they are the drivers of the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They produce the most jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know, when Senator Obama ended up his conversation with Joe the plumber — we need to spread the wealth around.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: In other words, we’re going to take Joe’s money, give it to Senator Obama, and let him spread the wealth around.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want Joe the plumber to spread that wealth around.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You told him you wanted to spread the wealth around.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The whole premise behind Senator Obama’s plans are class warfare, let’s spread the wealth around.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want small businesses — and by the way, the small businesses that we’re talking about would receive an increase in their taxes right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Who — why would you want to increase anybody’s taxes right now?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Why would you want to do that, anyone, anyone in America, when we have such a tough time, when these small business people, like Joe the plumber, are going to create jobs, unless you take that money from him and spread the wealth around.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Can I…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’re not going to do that in my administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If I can answer the question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number one, I want to cut taxes for 95 percent of Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, it is true that my friend and supporter, Warren Buffett, for example, could afford to pay a little more in taxes in order…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’re talking about Joe the plumber.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: OBAMA: … in order to give — in order to give additional tax cuts to Joe the plumber before he was at the point where he could make $250,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Then Exxon Mobil, which made $12 billion, record profits, over the last several quarters, they can afford to pay a little more so that ordinary families who are hurting out there — they’re trying to figure out how they’re going to afford food, how they’re going to save for their kids’ college education, they need a break.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So, look, nobody likes taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I would prefer that none of us had to pay taxes, including myself.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But ultimately, we’ve got to pay for the core investments that make this economy strong and somebody’s got to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Nobody likes taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s not raise anybody’s taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: OK?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I don’t mind paying a little more.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The fact is that businesses in America today are paying the second highest tax rate of anywhere in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Our tax rate for business in America is 35 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Ireland, it’s 11 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Where are companies going to go where they can create jobs and where they can do best in business?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to cut the business tax rate in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to encourage business.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, of all times in America, we need to cut people’s taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to encourage business, create jobs, not spread the wealth around.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, I think it’s important for the American public to understand that the $750 billion rescue package, if it’s structured properly, and, as president, I will make sure it’s structured properly, means that ultimately taxpayers get their money back, and that’s important to understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there is no doubt that we’ve been living beyond our means and we’re going to have to make some adjustments.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, what I’ve done throughout this campaign is to propose a net spending cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I haven’t made a promise about…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So let me get to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What I want to emphasize, though, is that I have been a strong proponent of pay-as- you-go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Every dollar that I’ve proposed, I’ve proposed an additional cut so that it matches.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And some of the cuts, just to give you an example, we spend $15 billion a year on subsidies to insurance companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It doesn’t — under the Medicare plan — it doesn’t help seniors get any better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s not improving our health care system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s just a giveaway.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We need to eliminate a whole host of programs that don’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I want to go through the federal budget line by line, page by page, programs that don’t work, we should cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Programs that we need, we should make them work better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, what is true is that Senator McCain and I have a difference in terms of the need to invest in America and the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I mentioned health care earlier.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we make investments now so that people have coverage, that we are preventing diseases, that will save on Medicare and Medicaid in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we invest in a serious energy policy, that will save in the amount of money we’re borrowing from China to send to Saudi Arabia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we invest now in our young people and their ability to go to college, that will allow them to drive this economy into the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what is absolutely true is that, once we get through this economic crisis and some of the specific proposals to get us out of this slump, that we’re not going to be able to go back to our profligate ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to have to embrace a culture and an ethic of responsibility, all of us, corporations, the federal government, and individuals out there who may be living beyond their means.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you, Bob.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I just want to get back to this home ownership.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: During the Depression era, we had a thing called the home ownership loan corporation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And they went out and bought up these mortgages.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And people were able to stay in their homes, and eventually the values of those homes went up, and they actually made money.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, by the way, this was a proposal made by Senator Clinton not too long ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So, obviously, if we can start increasing home values, then there will be creation of wealth.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But — OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: All right.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Energy — well, first — second of all, energy independence.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to have nuclear power.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to stop sending $700 billion a year to countries that don’t like us very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s wind, tide, solar, natural gas, nuclear, off-shore drilling, which Senator Obama has opposed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the point is that we become energy independent and we will create millions of jobs — millions of jobs in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: OK, what — what would I cut?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I would have, first of all, across-the-board spending freeze, OK?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Some people say that’s a hatchet.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s a hatchet, and then I would get out a scalpel, OK?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Because we’ve got — we have presided over the largest increase — we’ve got to have a new direction for this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have presided over the largest increase in government since the Great Society.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Government spending has gone completely out of control; $10 trillion dollar debt we’re giving to our kids, a half-a-trillion dollars we owe China.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know how to save billions of dollars in defense spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know how to eliminate programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought against — well, one of them would be the marketing assistance program.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Another one would be a number of subsidies for ethanol.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I oppose subsidies for ethanol because I thought it distorted the market and created inflation; Senator Obama supported those subsidies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I would eliminate the tariff on imported sugarcane-based ethanol from Brazil.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I know how to save billions.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I saved the taxpayer $6.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: 8 billion by fighting a deal for a couple of years, as you might recall, that was a sweetheart deal between an aircraft manufacturer, DOD, and people ended up in jail.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I would fight for a line-item veto, and I would certainly veto every earmark pork-barrel bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama has asked for nearly $1 billion in pork-barrel earmark projects…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: … including $3 million for an overhead projector in a planetarium in his hometown.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the way we cut — we’ll cut out all the pork.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, look, I think that we do have a disagreement about an across-the-board spending freeze.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It sounds good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s proposed periodically.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It doesn’t happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, in fact, an across-the-board spending freeze is a hatchet, and we do need a scalpel, because there are some programs that don’t work at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There are some programs that are underfunded.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I want to make sure that we are focused on those programs that work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator McCain talks a lot about earmarks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s one of the centerpieces of his campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Earmarks account for 0.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: 5 percent of the total federal budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There’s no doubt that the system needs reform and there are a lot of screwy things that we end up spending money on, and they need to be eliminated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But it’s not going to solve the problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, the last thing I think we have to focus on is a little bit of history, just so that we understand what we’re doing going forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When President Bush came into office, we had a budget surplus and the national debt was a little over $5 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It has doubled over the last eight years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we are now looking at a deficit of well over half a trillion dollars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So one of the things that I think we have to recognize is pursuing the same kinds of policies that we pursued over the last eight years is not going to bring down the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, frankly, Senator McCain voted for four out of five of President Bush’s budgets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to take this in a new direction, that’s what I propose as president.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Sure I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And let me tell you…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama, I am not President Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If you wanted to run against President Bush, you should have run four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to give a new direction to this economy in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama talks about voting for budgets.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He voted twice for a budget resolution that increases the taxes on individuals making $42,000 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Of course, we can take a hatchet and a scalpel to this budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s completely out of control.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The mayor of New York, Mayor Bloomberg, just imposed an across- the-board spending freeze on New York City.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They’re doing it all over America because they have to.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Because they have to balance their budgets.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I will balance our budgets and I will get them and I will…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: … reduce this — I can — we can do it with this kind of job creation of energy independence.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, look, Americans are hurting tonight and they’re angry and I understand that, and they want a new direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I can bring them in that direction by eliminating spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama talks about the budgets I voted for.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He voted for the last two budgets that had that $24 billion more in spending than the budget that the Bush administration proposed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He voted for the energy bill that was full of goodies for the oil companies that I opposed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So the fact is, let’s look at our records, Senator Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s look at it as graded by the National Taxpayers Union and the Citizens Against Government Waste and the other watchdog organizations.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought against spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought against special interests.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have fought for reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You have to tell me one time when you have stood up with the leaders of your party on one single major issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, there’s a lot of stuff that was put out there, so let me try to address it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: First of all, in terms of standing up to the leaders of my party, the first major bill that I voted on in the Senate was in support of tort reform, which wasn’t very popular with trial lawyers, a major constituency in the Democratic Party.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I support…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: An overwhelming vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I support charter schools and pay for performance for teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Doesn’t make me popular with the teachers union.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I support clean coal technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Doesn’t make me popular with environmentalists.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So I’ve got a history of reaching across the aisle.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now with respect to a couple of things Senator McCain said, the notion that I voted for a tax increase for people making $42,000 a year has been disputed by everybody who has looked at this claim that Senator McCain keeps on making.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Even FOX News disputes it, and that doesn’t happen very often when it comes to accusations about me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So the fact of the matter is that if I occasionally have mistaken your policies for George Bush’s policies, it’s because on the core economic issues that matter to the American people, on tax policy, on energy policy, on spending priorities, you have been a vigorous supporter of President Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, you’ve shown independence — commendable independence, on some key issues like torture, for example, and I give you enormous credit for that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But when it comes to economic policies, essentially what you’re proposing is eight more years of the same thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it hasn’t worked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think the American people understand it hasn’t worked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We need to move in a new direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let me just say, Bob.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But it’s very clear that I have disagreed with the Bush administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have disagreed with leaders of my own party.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got the scars to prove it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Whether it be bringing climate change to the floor of the Senate for the first time.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Whether it be opposition to spending and earmarks, whether it be the issue of torture, whether it be the conduct of the war in Iraq, which I vigorously opposed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Whether it be on fighting the pharmaceutical companies on Medicare prescription drugs, importation.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Whether it be fighting for an HMO patient’s bill of rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Whether it be the establishment of the 9/11 Commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have a long record of reform and fighting through on the floor of the United States Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama, your argument for standing up to the leadership of your party isn’t very convincing.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, this has been a tough campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s been a very tough campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I know from my experience in many campaigns that, if Senator Obama had asked — responded to my urgent request to sit down, and do town hall meetings, and come before the American people, we could have done at least 10 of them by now.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: When Senator Obama was first asked, he said, “Any place, any time,” the way Barry Goldwater and Jack Kennedy agreed to do, before the intervention of the tragedy at Dallas.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So I think the tone of this campaign could have been very different.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the fact is, it’s gotten pretty tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I regret some of the negative aspects of both campaigns.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the fact is that it has taken many turns which I think are unacceptable.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: One of them happened just the other day, when a man I admire and respect — I’ve written about him — Congressman John Lewis, an American hero, made allegations that Sarah Palin and I were somehow associated with the worst chapter in American history, segregation, deaths of children in church bombings, George Wallace.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That, to me, was so hurtful.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, Senator Obama, you didn’t repudiate those remarks.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Every time there’s been an out-of-bounds remark made by a Republican, no matter where they are, I have repudiated them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I hope that Senator Obama will repudiate those remarks that were made by Congressman John Lewis, very unfair and totally inappropriate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So I want to tell you, we will run a truthful campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This is a tough campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it’s a matter of fact that Senator Obama has spent more money on negative ads than any political campaign in history.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I can prove it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, Senator Obama, when he said — and he signed a piece of paper that said he would take public financing for his campaign if I did — that was back when he was a long-shot candidate — you didn’t keep your word.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And when you looked into the camera in a debate with Senator Clinton and said, “I will sit down and negotiate with John McCain about public financing before I make a decision,” you didn’t tell the American people the truth because you didn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that’s — that’s — that’s an unfortunate part.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now we have the highest spending by Senator Obama’s campaign than any time since Watergate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, look, you know, I think that we expect presidential campaigns to be tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think that, if you look at the record and the impressions of the American people — Bob, your network just did a poll, showing that two-thirds of the American people think that Senator McCain is running a negative campaign versus one-third of mine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And 100 percent, John, of your ads — 100 percent of them have been negative.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It absolutely is true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, now, I think the American people are less interested in our hurt feelings during the course of the campaign than addressing the issues that matter to them so deeply.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And there is nothing wrong with us having a vigorous debate like we’re having tonight about health care, about energy policy, about tax policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the stuff that campaigns should be made of.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The notion, though, that because we’re not doing town hall meetings that justifies some of the ads that have been going up, not just from your own campaign directly, John, but 527s and other organizations that make some pretty tough accusations, well, I don’t mind being attacked for the next three weeks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What the American people can’t afford, though, is four more years of failed economic policies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what they deserve over the next four weeks is that we talk about what’s most pressing to them: the economic crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain’s own campaign said publicly last week that, if we keep on talking about the economic crisis, we lose, so we need to change the subject.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I would love to see the next three weeks devoted to talking about the economy, devoted to talking about health care, devoted to talking about energy, and figuring out how the American people can send their kids to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that is something that I would welcome.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But it requires, I think, a recognition that politics as usual, as been practiced over the last several years, is not solving the big problems here in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, if you’ll turn on the television, as I — I watched the Arizona Cardinals defeat the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Congratulations.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Every other ad — ever other ad was an attack ad on my health care plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And any objective observer has said it’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You’re running ads right now that say that I oppose federal funding for stem cell research.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You’re running ads that misportray completely my position on immigration.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So the fact is that Senator Obama is spending unprecedented — unprecedented in the history of American politics, going back to the beginning, amounts of money in negative attack ads on me.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And of course, I’ve been talking about the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Of course, I’ve talked to people like Joe the plumber and tell him that I’m not going to spread his wealth around.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to let him keep his wealth.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And of course, we’re talking about positive plan of action to restore this economy and restore jobs in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s what my campaign is all about and that’s what it’ll continue to be all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But again, I did not hear a repudiation of Congressman…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I mean, look, if we want to talk about Congressman Lewis, who is an American hero, he, unprompted by my campaign, without my campaign’s awareness, made a statement that he was troubled with what he was hearing at some of the rallies that your running mate was holding, in which all the Republican reports indicated were shouting, when my name came up, things like “terrorist” and “kill him,” and that you’re running mate didn’t mention, didn’t stop, didn’t say “Hold on a second, that’s kind of out of line.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” And I think Congressman Lewis’ point was that we have to be careful about how we deal with our supporters.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to read what he said…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let — let — let… MCCAIN: You’ve got to read what he said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let me — let me complete…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … my response.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I do think that he inappropriately drew a comparison between what was happening there and what had happened during the civil rights movement, and we immediately put out a statement saying that we don’t think that comparison is appropriate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, in fact, afterwards, Congressman Lewis put out a similar statement, saying that he had probably gone over the line.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The important point here is, though, the American people have become so cynical about our politics, because all they see is a tit- for-tat and back-and-forth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what they want is the ability to just focus on some really big challenges that we face right now, and that’s what I have been trying to focus on this entire campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I cannot…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We can have serious differences about our health care policy, for example, John, because we do have a difference on health care policy, but we…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We do and I hope…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … talking about it this evening.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Sure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But when people suggest that I pal around with terrorists, then we’re not talking about issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What we’re talking about…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me just say I would…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let me just say categorically I’m proud of the people that come to our rallies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Whenever you get a large rally of 10,000, 15,000, 20,000 people, you’re going to have some fringe peoples.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve — and we’ve always said that that’s not appropriate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But to somehow say that group of young women who said “Military wives for McCain” are somehow saying anything derogatory about you, but anything — and those veterans that wear those hats that say “World War II, Vietnam, Korea, Iraq,” I’m not going to stand for people saying that the people that come to my rallies are anything but the most dedicated, patriotic men and women that are in this nation and they’re great citizens.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’m not going to stand for somebody saying that because someone yelled something at a rally — there’s a lot of things that have been yelled at your rallies, Senator Obama, that I’m not happy about either.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: In fact, some T-shirts that are very…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: John, I…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: … unacceptable.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So the point is — the point is that I have repudiated every time someone’s been out of line, whether they’ve been part of my campaign or not, and I will continue to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But the fact is that we need to absolutely not stand for the kind of things that have been going on.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I haven’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, look, Bob, as I said…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, here’s what I would say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I mean, we can have a debate back and forth about the merits of each other’s campaigns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I suspect we won’t agree here tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What I think is most important is that we recognize that to solve the key problems that we’re facing, if we’re going to solve two wars, the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression, if we can — if we’re going to focus on lifting wages that have declined over the last eight years and create jobs here in America, then Democrats, independents and Republicans, we’re going to have to be able to work together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what is important is making sure that we disagree without being disagreeable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it means that we can have tough, vigorous debates around issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What we can’t do, I think, is try to characterize each other as bad people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that has been a culture in Washington that has been taking place for too long.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, Bob, you asked me a direct question.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Yes, real quick.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Ayers, I don’t care about an old washed-up terrorist.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But as Senator Clinton said in her debates with you, we need to know the full extent of that relationship.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to know the full extent of Senator Obama’s relationship with ACORN, who is now on the verge of maybe perpetrating one of the greatest frauds in voter history in this country, maybe destroying the fabric of democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The same front outfit organization that your campaign gave $832,000 for “lighting and site selection.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” So all of these things need to be examined, of course.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Bob, I think it’s going to be important to just — I’ll respond to these two particular allegations that Senator McCain has made and that have gotten a lot of attention.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In fact, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Ayers has become the centerpiece of Senator McCain’s campaign over the last two or three weeks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This has been their primary focus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So let’s get the record straight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Bill Ayers is a professor of education in Chicago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Forty years ago, when I was 8 years old, he engaged in despicable acts with a radical domestic group.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I have roundly condemned those acts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Ten years ago he served and I served on a school reform board that was funded by one of Ronald Reagan’s former ambassadors and close friends, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Annenberg.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Other members on that board were the presidents of the University of Illinois, the president of Northwestern University, who happens to be a Republican, the president of The Chicago Tribune, a Republican- leaning newspaper.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Ayers is not involved in my campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He has never been involved in this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And he will not advise me in the White House.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So that’s Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Ayers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, with respect to ACORN, ACORN is a community organization.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Apparently what they’ve done is they were paying people to go out and register folks, and apparently some of the people who were out there didn’t really register people, they just filled out a bunch of names.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It had nothing to do with us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We were not involved.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The only involvement I’ve had with ACORN was I represented them alongside the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Justice Department in making Illinois implement a motor voter law that helped people get registered at DMVs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, the reason I think that it’s important to just get these facts out is because the allegation that Senator McCain has continually made is that somehow my associations are troubling.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you who I associate with.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: On economic policy, I associate with Warren Buffett and former Fed Chairman Paul Volcker.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If I’m interested in figuring out my foreign policy, I associate myself with my running mate, Joe Biden or with Dick Lugar, the Republican ranking member on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, or General Jim Jones, the former supreme allied commander of NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Those are the people, Democrats and Republicans, who have shaped my ideas and who will be surrounding me in the White House.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think the fact that this has become such an important part of your campaign, Senator McCain, says more about your campaign than it says about me.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, again, while you were on the board of the Woods Foundation, you and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Ayers, together, you sent $230,000 to ACORN.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So — and you launched your political campaign in Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Ayers’ living room.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s absolutely not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the facts are facts and records are records.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s not the facts.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it’s not the fact — it’s not the fact that Senator Obama chooses to associate with a guy who in 2001 said that he wished he had have bombed more, and he had a long association with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s the fact that all the — all of the details need to be known about Senator Obama’s relationship with them and with ACORN and the American people will make a judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And my campaign is about getting this economy back on track, about creating jobs, about a brighter future for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what my campaign is about and I’m not going to raise taxes the way Senator Obama wants to raise taxes in a tough economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that’s really what this campaign is going to be about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Joe Biden, I think, is one of the finest public servants that has served in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s not just that he has some of the best foreign policy credentials of anybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And Democrats and Republicans alike, I think, acknowledge his expertise there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But it’s also that his entire life he has never forgotten where he came from, coming from Scranton, fighting on behalf of working families, remembering what it’s like to see his father lose his job and go through a downward spiral economically.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, as a consequence, his consistent pattern throughout his career is to fight for the little guy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what he’s done when it comes to economic policies that will help working families get a leg up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what he’s done when it comes to, for example, passing the landmark 1994 crime bill, the Violence Against Women’s Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Joe has always made sure that he is fighting on behalf of working families, and I think he shares my core values and my sense of where the country needs to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because after eight years of failed policies, he and I both agree that what we’re going to have to do is to reprioritize, make sure that we’re investing in the American people, give tax cuts not to the wealthiest corporations, but give them to small businesses and give them to individuals who are struggling right now, make sure that we finally get serious about energy independence, something that has been languishing in Washington for 30 years, and make sure that our kids get a great education and can afford to go to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So, on the key issues that are of importance to American families, Joe Biden’s always been on the right side, and I think he will make an outstanding president if, heaven forbid, something happened to me.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, Americans have gotten to know Sarah Palin.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They know that she’s a role model to women and other — and reformers all over America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She’s a reformer.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She is — she took on a governor who was a member of her own party when she ran for governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: When she was the head of their energy and natural resources board, she saw corruption, she resigned and said, “This can’t go on.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” She’s given money back to the taxpayers.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She’s cut the size of government.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She negotiated with the oil companies and faced them down, a $40 billion pipeline of natural gas that’s going to relieve the energy needs of the United — of what they call the lower 48.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She’s a reformer through and through.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it’s time we had that bresh of freth air — breath of fresh air coming into our nation’s capital and sweep out the old-boy network and the cronyism that’s been so much a part of it that I’ve fought against for all these years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She’ll be my partner.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She understands reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And, by the way, she also understands special-needs families.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She understands that autism is on the rise, that we’ve got to find out what’s causing it, and we’ve got to reach out to these families, and help them, and give them the help they need as they raise these very special needs children.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She understands that better than almost any American that I know.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m proud of her.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And she has ignited our party and people all over America that have never been involved in the political process.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I can’t tell how proud I am of her and her family.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Her husband’s a pretty tough guy, by the way, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, I think it’s — that’s going to be up to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think that, obviously, she’s a capable politician who has, I think, excited the — a base in the Republican Party.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think it’s very commendable the work she’s done on behalf of special needs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I agree with that, John.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I do want to just point out that autism, for example, or other special needs will require some additional funding, if we’re going to get serious in terms of research.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That is something that every family that advocates on behalf of disabled children talk about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if we have an across-the-board spending freeze, we’re not going to be able to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s an example of, I think, the kind of use of the scalpel that we want to make sure that we’re funding some of those programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think that Joe Biden is qualified in many respects.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I do point out that he’s been wrong on many foreign policy and national security issues, which is supposed to be his strength.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He voted against the first Gulf War.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He voted against it and, obviously, we had to take Saddam Hussein out of Kuwait or it would’ve threatened the Middle Eastern world supply.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: In Iraq, he had this cockamamie idea about dividing Iraq into three countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’re seeing Iraq united as Iraqis, tough, hard, but we’re seeing them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’re now about to have an agreement for status of forces in Iraq coming up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There are several issues in which, frankly, Joe Biden and I openly and honestly disagreed on national security policy, and he’s been wrong on a number of the major ones.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But again, I want to come back to, notice every time Senator Obama says, “We need to spend more, we need to spend more, that’s the answer” — why do we always have to spend more?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Why can’t we have transparency, accountability, reform of these agencies of government?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Maybe that’s why he’s asked for 860 — sought and proposed $860 billion worth of new spending and wants to raise people’s taxes in a time of incredible challenge and difficulty and heartache for the American families.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Climate change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think that in ten years, we can reduce our dependence so that we no longer have to import oil from the Middle East or Venezuela.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s about a realistic timeframe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is the most important issue that our future economy is going to face.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Obviously, we’ve got an immediate crisis right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But nothing is more important than us no longer borrowing $700 billion or more from China and sending it to Saudi Arabia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s mortgaging our children’s future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, from the start of this campaign, I’ve identified this as one of my top priorities and here is what I think we have to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number one, we do need to expand domestic production and that means, for example, telling the oil companies the 68 million acres that they currently have leased that they’re not drilling, use them or lose them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think that we should look at offshore drilling and implement it in a way that allows us to get some additional oil.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But understand, we only have three to four percent of the world’s oil reserves and we use 25 percent of the world’s oil, which means that we can’t drill our way out of the problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I’ve focused on putting resources into solar, wind, biodiesel, geothermal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: These have been priorities of mine since I got to the Senate, and it is absolutely critical that we develop a high fuel efficient car that’s built not in Japan and not in South Korea, but built here in the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We invented the auto industry and the fact that we have fallen so far behind is something that we have to work on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now I just want to make one last point because Senator McCain mentioned NAFTA and the issue of trade and that actually bears on this issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I believe in free trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I also believe that for far too long, certainly during the course of the Bush administration with the support of Senator McCain, the attitude has been that any trade agreement is a good trade agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And NAFTA doesn’t have — did not have enforceable labor agreements and environmental agreements.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what I said was we should include those and make them enforceable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In the same way that we should enforce rules against China manipulating its currency to make our exports more expensive and their exports to us cheaper.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when it comes to South Korea, we’ve got a trade agreement up right now, they are sending hundreds of thousands of South Korean cars into the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s all good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We can only get 4,000 to 5,000 into South Korea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That is not free trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to have a president who is going to be advocating on behalf of American businesses and American workers and I make no apology for that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, you know, I admire so much Senator Obama’s eloquence.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And you really have to pay attention to words.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He said, we will look at offshore drilling.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Did you get that?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look at.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We can offshore drill now.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to do it now.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We will reduce the cost of a barrel of oil because we show the world that we have a supply of our own.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s doable.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The technology is there and we have to drill now.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, on the subject of free trade agreements.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I am a free trader.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I need — we need to have education and training programs for displaced workers that work, going to our community colleges.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But let me give you another example of a free trade agreement that Senator Obama opposes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Right now, because of previous agreements, some made by President Clinton, the goods and products that we send to Colombia, which is our largest agricultural importer of our products, is — there’s a billion dollars that we — our businesses have paid so far in order to get our goods in there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Because of previous agreements, their goods and products come into our country for free.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So Senator Obama, who has never traveled south of our border, opposes the Colombia Free Trade Agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The same country that’s helping us try to stop the flow of drugs into our country that’s killing young Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And also the country that just freed three Americans that will help us create jobs in America because they will be a market for our goods and products without having to pay — without us having to pay the billions of dollars — the billion dollars and more that we’ve already paid.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Free trade with Colombia is something that’s a no-brainer.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But maybe you ought to travel down there and visit them and maybe you could understand it a lot better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let me respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Actually, I understand it pretty well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The history in Colombia right now is that labor leaders have been targeted for assassination on a fairly consistent basis and there have not been prosecutions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what I have said, because the free trade — the trade agreement itself does have labor and environmental protections, but we have to stand for human rights and we have to make sure that violence isn’t being perpetrated against workers who are just trying to organize for their rights, which is why, for example, I supported the Peruvian Free Trade Agreement which was a well-structured agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I think that the important point is we’ve got to have a president who understands the benefits of free trade but also is going to enforce unfair trade agreements and is going to stand up to other countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the last point I’ll make, because we started on energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When I talked about the automakers, they are obviously getting hammered right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They were already having a tough time because of high gas prices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And now with the financial crisis, car dealerships are closing and people can’t get car loans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I think it’s important for us to get loan guarantees to the automakers, but we do have to hold them responsible as well to start producing the highly fuel-efficient cars of the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And Detroit had dragged its feet too long in terms of getting that done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to be one of my highest priorities because transportation accounts for about 30 percent of our total energy consumption.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we can get that right, then we can move in a direction not only of energy independence, but we can create 5 million new jobs all across America, including in the heartland where we can retool some of these plants to make these highly fuel-efficient cars and also to make wind turbines and solar panels, the kinds of clean energy approaches that should be the driver of our economy for the next century.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me just said that that this is — he — Senator Obama doesn’t want a free trade agreement with our best ally in the region but wants to sit down across the table without precondition to — with Hugo Chavez, the guy who has been helping FARC, the terrorist organization.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Free trade between ourselves and Colombia, I just recited to you the benefits of concluding that agreement, a billion dollars of American dollars that could have gone to creating jobs and businesses in the United States, opening up those markets.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So I don’t — I don’t think there’s any doubt that Senator Obama wants to restrict trade and he wants to raise taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the last president of the United States that tried that was Herbert Hoover, and we went from a deep recession into a depression.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’re not going to follow that path while I’m — when I’m president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to do both, and that’s exactly what my plan does.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, as I travel around the country, this is the issue that will break your heart over and over again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Just yesterday, I was in Toledo shaking some hands in a line.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Two women, both of them probably in their mid- to late-50s, had just been laid off of their plant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Neither of them have health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And they were desperate for some way of getting coverage, because, understandably, they’re worried that, if they get sick, they could go bankrupt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So here’s what my plan does.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you have health insurance, then you don’t have to do anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you’ve got health insurance through your employer, you can keep your health insurance, keep your choice of doctor, keep your plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The only thing we’re going to try to do is lower costs so that those cost savings are passed onto you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we estimate we can cut the average family’s premium by about $2,500 per year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you don’t have health insurance, then what we’re going to do is to provide you the option of buying into the same kind of federal pool that both Senator McCain and I enjoy as federal employees, which will give you high-quality care, choice of doctors, at lower costs, because so many people are part of this insured group.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to make sure that insurance companies can’t discriminate on the basis of pre-existing conditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ll negotiate with the drug companies for the cheapest available price on drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We are going to invest in information technology to eliminate bureaucracy and make the system more efficient.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we are going to make sure that we manage chronic illnesses, like diabetes and heart disease, that cost a huge amount, but could be prevented.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to put more money into preventive care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This will cost some money on the front end, but over the long term this is the only way that not only are we going to make families healthy, but it’s also how we’re going to save the federal budget, because we can’t afford these escalating costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, it is a terribly painful situation for Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They’re seeing their premiums, their co-pays go up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Forty-seven million Americans are without health insurance in America today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it really is the cost, the escalating costs of health care that are inflicting such pain on working families and people across this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I am convinced we need to do a lot of things.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to put health care records online.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The V.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: does that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
