transcript_turns.text: That will — that will reduce costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to have more community health centers.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to have walk-in clinics.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The rise of obesity amongst young Americans is one of the most alarming statistics that there is.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We should have physical fitness programs and nutrition programs in schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Every parent should know what’s going on there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We — we need to have — we need to have employers reward employees who join health clubs and practice wellness and fitness.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I want to give every American family a $5,000 refundable tax credit.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Take it and get anywhere in America the health care that you wish.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, my old buddy, Joe, Joe the plumber, is out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, Joe, Senator Obama’s plan, if you’re a small business and you are able — and your — the guy that sells to you will not have his capital gains tax increase, which Senator Obama wants, if you’re out there, my friend, and you’ve got employees, and you’ve got kids, if you don’t get — adopt the health care plan that Senator Obama mandates, he’s going to fine you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, Senator Obama, I’d like — still like to know what that fine is going to be, and I don’t think that Joe right now wants to pay a fine when he is seeing such difficult times in America’s economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama wants to set up health care bureaucracies, take over the health care of America through — as he said, his object is a single payer system.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If you like that, you’ll love Canada and England.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So the point is…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is not and I just described it…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: No, you stated it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I just…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Excuse me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I just described what my plan is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’m happy to talk to you, Joe, too, if you’re out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Here’s your fine — zero.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You won’t pay a fine, because…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Zero?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Zero, because as I said in our last debate and I’ll repeat, John, I exempt small businesses from the requirement for large businesses that can afford to provide health care to their employees, but are not doing it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I exempt small businesses from having to pay into a kitty.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But large businesses that can afford it, we’ve got a choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Either they provide health insurance to their employees or somebody has to.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Right now, what happens is those employees get dumped into either the Medicaid system, which taxpayers pick up, or they’re going to the emergency room for uncompensated care, which everybody picks up in their premiums.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The average family is paying an additional $900 a year in higher premiums because of the uninsured.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So here’s what we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We exempt small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In fact, what, Joe, if you want to do the right thing with your employees and you want to provide them health insurance, we’ll give you a 50 percent credit so that you will actually be able to afford it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you don’t have health insurance or you want to buy into a group plan, you will be able to buy into the plan that I just described.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, what we haven’t talked about is Senator McCain’s plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He says he’s going to give you all a $5,000 tax credit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That sounds pretty good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And you can go out and buy your own insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Here’s the problem — that for about 20 million people, you may find yourselves no longer having employer-based health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is because younger people might be able to get health insurance for $5,000, young and healthy folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Older folks, less healthy folks, what’s going to end up happening is that you’re going to be the only ones left in your employer-based system, your employers won’t be able to afford it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And once you’re out on your own with this $5,000 credit, Senator McCain, for the first time, is going to be taxing the health care benefits that you have from your employer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is your plan, John.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: For the first time in history, you will be taxing people’s health care benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: By the way, the average policy costs about $12,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So if you’ve got $5,000 and it’s going to cost you $12,000, that’s a loss for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Last point about Senator McCain’s plan is that insurers right now, the main restrictions on what they do is primarily state law and, under Senator McCain’s plan, those rules would be stripped away and you would start seeing a lot more insurance companies cherry-picking and excluding people from coverage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That, I think, is a mistake and I think that this is a fundamental difference in our campaign and how we would approach health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Hey, Joe, you’re rich, congratulations, because what Joe wanted to do was buy the business that he’s been working for 10-12 hours a day, seven days a week, and you said that you wanted to spread the wealth, but — in other words, take Joe’s money and then you decide what to do with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, Joe, you’re rich, congratulations, and you will then fall into the category where you’ll have to pay a fine if you don’t provide health insurance that Senator Obama mandates, not the kind that you think is best for your family, your children, your employees, but the kind that he mandates for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s big government at its best.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, 95 percent of the people in America will receive more money under my plan because they will receive not only their present benefits, which may be taxed, which will be taxed, but then you add $5,000 onto it, except for those people who have the gold-plated Cadillac insurance policies that have to do with cosmetic surgery and transplants and all of those kinds of things.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And the good thing about this is they’ll be able to go across America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: The average cost of a health care insurance plan in America today is $5,800.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to give them $5,000 to take with them wherever they want to go, and this will give them affordability.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This will give them availability.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This will give them a chance to choose their own futures, not have Senator Obama and government decide that for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This really gets down to the fundamental difference in our philosophies.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: If you notice that in all of this proposal, Senator — government wants — Senator Obama wants government to do the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama wants government to do the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want, Joe, you to do the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want to leave money in your pocket.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I want you to be able to choose the health care for you and your family.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I’m all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got too much government and too much spending and the government is — the size of government has grown by 40 percent in the last eight years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We can’t afford that in the next eight years and Senator Obama, with the Democrats in charge of Congress, things have gotten worse.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Have you noticed, they’ve been in charge the last two years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Very briefly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You all just heard my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you’ve got an employer-based health care plan, you keep it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, under Senator McCain’s plan there is a strong risk that people would lose their employer-based health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the choice you’ll have is having your employer no longer provide you health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And don’t take my word for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Chamber of Commerce, which generally doesn’t support a lot of Democrats, said that this plan could lead to the unraveling of the employer-based health care system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: All I want to do, if you’ve already got health care, is lower your costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That includes you, Joe.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I would never and have never in all the years I’ve been there imposed a litmus test on any nominee to the court.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s not appropriate to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I thought it was a bad decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think there were a lot of decisions that were bad.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think that decisions should rest in the hands of the states.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m a federalist.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I believe strongly that we should have nominees to the United States Supreme Court based on their qualifications rather than any litmus test.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, let me say that there was a time a few years ago when the United States Senate was about to blow up.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Republicans wanted to have just a majority vote to confirm a judge and the Democrats were blocking in an unprecedented fashion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We got together seven Republicans, seven Democrats.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You were offered a chance to join.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You chose not to because you were afraid of the appointment of, quote, “conservative judges.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” I voted for Justice Breyer and Justice Ginsburg.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Not because I agreed with their ideology, but because I thought they were qualified and that elections have consequences when presidents are nominated.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: This is a very important issue we’re talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama voted against Justice Breyer and Justice Roberts on the grounds that they didn’t meet his ideological standards.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the way we should judge these nominees.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Elections have consequences.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They should be judged on their qualifications.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And so that’s what I will do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I will find the best people in the world — in the United States of America who have a history of strict adherence to the Constitution.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And not legislating from the bench.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I would consider anyone in their qualifications.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I do not believe that someone who has supported Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Wade that would be part of those qualifications.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I certainly would not impose any litmus test.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think it’s true that we shouldn’t apply a strict litmus test and the most important thing in any judge is their capacity to provide fairness and justice to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it is true that this is going to be, I think, one of the most consequential decisions of the next president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is very likely that one of us will be making at least one and probably more than one appointments and Roe versus Wade probably hangs in the balance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now I would not provide a litmus test.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I am somebody who believes that Roe versus Wade was rightly decided.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think that abortion is a very difficult issue and it is a moral issue and one that I think good people on both sides can disagree on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what ultimately I believe is that women in consultation with their families, their doctors, their religious advisers, are in the best position to make this decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think that the Constitution has a right to privacy in it that shouldn’t be subject to state referendum, any more than our First Amendment rights are subject to state referendum, any more than many of the other rights that we have should be subject to popular vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So this is going to be an important issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I will look for those judges who have an outstanding judicial record, who have the intellect, and who hopefully have a sense of what real-world folks are going through.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ll just give you one quick example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain and I disagreed recently when the Supreme Court made it more difficult for a woman named Lilly Ledbetter to press her claim for pay discrimination.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: For years, she had been getting paid less than a man had been paid for doing the exact same job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when she brought a suit, saying equal pay for equal work, the judges said, well, you know, it’s taken you too long to bring this lawsuit, even though she didn’t know about it until fairly recently.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We tried to overturn it in the Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I supported that effort to provide better guidance to the courts; John McCain opposed it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think that it’s important for judges to understand that if a woman is out there trying to raise a family, trying to support her family, and is being treated unfairly, then the court has to stand up, if nobody else will.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the kind of judge that I want.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Obviously, that law waived the statute of limitations, which you could have gone back 20 or 30 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It was a trial lawyer’s dream.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let me talk to you about an important aspect of this issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to change the culture of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Those of us who are proudly pro-life understand that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it’s got to be courage and compassion that we show to a young woman who’s facing this terribly difficult decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Senator Obama, as a member of the Illinois State Senate, voted in the Judiciary Committee against a law that would provide immediate medical attention to a child born of a failed abortion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He voted against that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And then, on the floor of the State Senate, as he did 130 times as a state senator, he voted present.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Then there was another bill before the Senate Judiciary Committee in the state of Illinois not that long ago, where he voted against a ban on partial-birth abortion, one of the late-term abortion, a really — one of the bad procedures, a terrible.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And then, on the floor of the Illinois State Senate, he voted present.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know how you vote “present” on some of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know how you align yourself with the extreme aspect of the pro- abortion movement in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that’s his record, and that’s a matter of his record.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And he’ll say it has something to do with Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Wade, about the Illinois State Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It was clear-cut votes that Senator Obama voted, I think, in direct contradiction to the feelings and views of mainstream America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Yes, let me respond to this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If it sounds incredible that I would vote to withhold lifesaving treatment from an infant, that’s because it’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The — here are the facts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There was a bill that was put forward before the Illinois Senate that said you have to provide lifesaving treatment and that would have helped to undermine Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Wade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The fact is that there was already a law on the books in Illinois that required providing lifesaving treatment, which is why not only myself but pro-choice Republicans and Democrats voted against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the Illinois Medical Society, the organization of doctors in Illinois, voted against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Their Hippocratic Oath would have required them to provide care, and there was already a law in the books.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: With respect to partial-birth abortion, I am completely supportive of a ban on late-term abortions, partial-birth or otherwise, as long as there’s an exception for the mother’s health and life, and this did not contain that exception.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I attempted, as many have in the past, of including that so that it is constitutional.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that was rejected, and that’s why I voted present, because I’m willing to support a ban on late-term abortions as long as we have that exception.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The last point I want to make on the issue of abortion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This is an issue that — look, it divides us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And in some ways, it may be difficult to — to reconcile the two views.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there surely is some common ground when both those who believe in choice and those who are opposed to abortion can come together and say, “We should try to prevent unintended pregnancies by providing appropriate education to our youth, communicating that sexuality is sacred and that they should not be engaged in cavalier activity, and providing options for adoption, and helping single mothers if they want to choose to keep the baby.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” Those are all things that we put in the Democratic platform for the first time this year, and I think that’s where we can find some common ground, because nobody’s pro-abortion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s always a tragic situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We should try to reduce these circumstances.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Just again…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Just again, the example of the eloquence of Senator Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: He’s health for the mother.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You know, that’s been stretched by the pro-abortion movement in America to mean almost anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s the extreme pro-abortion position, quote, “health.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: ” But, look, Cindy and I are adoptive parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We know what a treasure and joy it is to have an adopted child in our lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We’ll do everything we can to improve adoption in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But that does not mean that we will cease to protect the rights of the unborn.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Of course, we have to come together.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Of course, we have to work together, and, of course, it’s vital that we do so and help these young women who are facing such a difficult decision, with a compassion, that we’ll help them with the adoptive services, with the courage to bring that child into this world and we’ll help take care of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This probably has more to do with our economic future than anything and that means it also has a national security implication, because there’s never been a nation on earth that saw its economy decline and continued to maintain its primacy as a military power.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve got to get our education system right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, typically, what’s happened is that there’s been a debate between more money or reform, and I think we need both.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In some cases, we are going to have to invest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Early childhood education, which closes the achievement gap, so that every child is prepared for school, every dollar we invest in that, we end up getting huge benefits with improved reading scores, reduced dropout rates, reduced delinquency rates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s going to be critically important for us to recruit a generation of new teachers, an army of new teachers, especially in math and science, give them higher pay, give them more professional development and support in exchange for higher standards and accountability.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think it’s important for us to make college affordable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Right now, I meet young people all across the country who either have decided not to go to college or if they’re going to college, they are taking on $20,000, $30,000, $50,000, $60,000 worth of debt, and it’s very difficult for them to go into some fields, like basic research in science, for example, thinking to themselves that they’re going to have a mortgage before they even buy a house.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I’ve proposed a $4,000 tuition credit, every student, every year, in exchange for some form of community service, whether it’s military service, whether it’s Peace Corps, whether it’s working in a community.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If we do those things, then I believe that we can create a better school system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there’s one last ingredient that I just want to mention, and that’s parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We can’t do it just in the schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Parents are going to have to show more responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They’ve got to turn off the TV set, put away the video games, and, finally, start instilling that thirst for knowledge that our students need.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, it’s the civil rights issue of the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: There’s no doubt that we have achieved equal access to schools in America after a long and difficult and terrible struggle.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But what is the advantage in a low income area of sending a child to a failed school and that being your only choice?

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So choice and competition amongst schools is one of the key elements that’s already been proven in places in like New Orleans and New York City and other places, where we have charter schools, where we take good teachers and we reward them and promote them.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we find bad teachers another line of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we have to be able to give parents the same choice, frankly, that Senator Obama and Mrs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Obama had and Cindy and I had to send our kids to the school — their kids to the school of their choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Charter schools aren’t the only answer, but they’re providing competition.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: They are providing the kind of competitions that have upgraded both schools — types of schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now, throwing money at the problem is not the answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: You will find that some of the worst school systems in America get the most money per student.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: So I believe that we need to reward these good teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to encourage programs such as Teach for America and Troops to Teachers where people, after having served in the military, can go right to teaching and not have to take these examinations which — or have the certification that some are required in some states.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Look, we must improve education in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: As far as college education is concerned, we need to make those student loans available.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to give them a repayment schedule that they can meet.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to have full student loan program for in-state tuition.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we certainly need to adjust the certain loan eligibility to inflation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, we have a tradition of local control of the schools and that’s a tradition that has served us well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I do think that it is important for the federal government to step up and help local school districts do some of the things they need to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now we tried to do this under President Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He put forward No Child Left Behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Unfortunately, they left the money behind for No Child Left Behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And local school districts end up having more of a burden, a bunch of unfunded mandates, the same kind of thing that happened with special education where we did the right thing by saying every school should provide education to kids with special needs, but we never followed through on the promise of funding, and that left local school districts very cash-strapped.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So what I want to do is focus on early childhood education, providing teachers higher salaries in exchange for more support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain and I actually agree on two things that he just mentioned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Charter schools, I doubled the number of charter schools in Illinois despite some reservations from teachers unions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s important to foster competition inside the public schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we also agree on the need for making sure that if we have bad teachers that they are swiftly — after given an opportunity to prove themselves, if they can’t hack it, then we need to move on because our kids have to have their best future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Where we disagree is on the idea that we can somehow give out vouchers — give vouchers as a way of securing the problems in our education system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I also have to disagree on Senator McCain’s record when it comes to college accessibility and affordability.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Recently his key economic adviser was asked about why he didn’t seem to have some specific programs to help young people go to college and the response was, well, you know, we can’t give money to every interest group that comes along.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think America’s youth are interest groups, I think they’re our future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is an example of where we are going to have to prioritize.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We can’t say we’re going to do things and then not explain in concrete terms how we’re going to pay for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if we’re going to do some of the things you mentioned, like lowering loan rates or what have you, somebody has got to pay for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s not going to happen on its own.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, sure.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’m sure you’re aware, Senator Obama, of the program in the Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: , school system where vouchers are provided and there’s a certain number, I think it’s a thousand and some and some 9,000 parents asked to be eligible for that.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Because they wanted to have the same choice that you and I and Cindy and your wife have had.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And that is because they wanted to choose the school that they thought was best for their children.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we all know the state of the Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: , school system.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That was vouchers.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That was vouchers, Senator Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’m frankly surprised you didn’t pay more attention to that example.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Now as far as the No Child Left Behind is concerned, it was a great first beginning in my view.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It had its flaws, it had its problems, the first time we had looked at the issue of education in America from a nationwide perspective.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we need to fix a lot of the problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to sit down and reauthorize it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But, again, spending more money isn’t always the answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think the Head Start program is a great program.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: A lot of people, including me, said, look, it’s not doing what it should do.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: By the third grade many times children who were in the Head Start program aren’t any better off than the others.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s reform it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Let’s reform it and fund it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That was, of course, out-of-bounds by the Democrats.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to reform these programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to have transparency.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We need to have rewards.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: It’s a system that cries out for accountability and transparency and the adequate funding.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I just said to you earlier, town hall meeting after town hall meeting, parents come with kids, children — precious children who have autism.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Sarah Palin knows about that better than most.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll find and we’ll spend the money, research, to find the cause of autism.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll care for these young children.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And all Americans will open their wallets and their hearts to do so.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But to have a situation, as you mentioned in our earlier comments, that the most expensive education in the world is in the United States of America also means that it cries out for reform, as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I will support those reforms, and I will fund the ones that are reformed.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: But I’m not going to continue to throw money at a problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve got to tell you that vouchers, where they are requested and where they are agreed to, are a good and workable system.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it’s been proven.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ll just make a quick comment about vouchers in D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Senator McCain’s absolutely right: The D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: school system is in terrible shape, and it has been for a very long time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got a wonderful new superintendent there who’s working very hard with the young mayor there to try…

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Who supports vouchers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … who initiated — actually, supports charters.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: She supports vouchers, also.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But the — but here’s the thing, is that, even if Senator McCain were to say that vouchers were the way to go — I disagree with him on this, because the data doesn’t show that it actually solves the problem — the centerpiece of Senator McCain’s education policy is to increase the voucher program in D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: by 2,000 slots.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That leaves all of you who live in the other 50 states without an education reform policy from Senator McCain.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So if we are going to be serious about this issue, we’ve got to have a president who is going to tackle it head-on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what I intend to do as president.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Because there’s not enough vouchers; therefore, we shouldn’t do it, even though it’s working.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I got it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you again, Bob.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Thanks to Hofstra.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And it’s great to be with you again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I think we’ve had a very healthy discussion.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: My friends, as I said in my opening remarks, these are very difficult times and challenges for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And they were graphically demonstrated again today.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: America needs a new direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We cannot be satisfied with what we’ve been doing for the last eight years.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I have a record of reform, and taking on my party, the other party, the special interests, whether it be an HMO Patients’ Bill of Rights, or trying to clean up the campaign finance system in — in this country, or whether it be establishment of a 9/11 Commission, I have a long record of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve been a careful steward of your tax dollars.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to make health care affordable and available.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to make quality education there for all of our citizens, not just the privileged few.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to stop the spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: We have to stop the spending, which has mortgaged your children’s futures.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: All of these things and all the promises and commitments that Senator Obama and I made made to you tonight will base — will be based on whether you can trust us or not to be careful stewards of your tax dollar, to make sure America is safe and secure and prosperous, to make sure we reform the institutions of government.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I’ve asked you not only to examine my record, but my proposals for the future of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’ve spent my entire life in the service of this nation and putting my country first.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: Thereâ€™s a long line of McCains that have served our country for a long time in war and in peace, it’s been the great honor of my life, and I’ve been proud to serve.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: And I hope you’ll give me an opportunity to serve again.

transcript_turns.speaker: John McCain
transcript_turns.text: I’d be honored and humbled.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I want to thank Senator McCain and Bob for moderating.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think we all know America is going through tough times right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The policies of the last eight years and — and Washington’s unwillingness to tackle the tough problems for decades has left us in the worst economic crisis since the Great Depression.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why the biggest risk we could take right now is to adopt the same failed policies and the same failed politics that we’ve seen over the last eight years and somehow expect a different result.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We need fundamental change in this country, and that’s what I’d like to bring.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, over the last 20 months, you’ve invited me into your homes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’ve shared your stories with me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And you’ve confirmed once again the fundamental decency and generosity of the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I’m sure that our brighter days are still ahead.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we’re going to have to invest in the American people again, in tax cuts for the middle class, in health care for all Americans, and college for every young person who wants to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In businesses that can create the new energy economy of the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In policies that will lift wages and will grow our middle class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: These are the policies I have fought for my entire career.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And these are the policies I want to bring to the White House.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But it’s not going to be easy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s not going to be quick.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It is going to be requiring all of us — Democrats, Republicans, independents — to come together and to renew a spirit of sacrifice and service and responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m absolutely convinced we can do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I would ask for your vote, and I promise you that if you give me the extraordinary honor of serving as your president, I will work every single day, tirelessly, on your behalf and on the behalf of the future of our children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much.
